products.name: Brokerage income
products.note: Revenue from brokerage activities is accounted for on point in time when performance obligation is satisfied i.e. the trade date of transaction.

products.name: Fees and other charges
products.note: Income from fees and other charges, viz login fee, pre-payment charges etc., are recognised on a point-in-time basis and are recorded when realised.

products.name: Portfolio management fees
products.note: Income from portfolio management fees is recognised over the period of the agreement in terms of which services are performed.

products.name: Dividend income
products.note: Dividend income is recognised in profit or loss when the Group's right to receive payment of the dividend is established.

products.name: Rental income
products.note: Rental income is recognized over a period of time as and when accrued as per the terms of the contract.

products.name: Income from trading in securities
products.note: Income from trading in securities is accounted for when the control of the securities is passed on to the customer, which is generally on sale of securities or at the time of redemption in case of bonds.

products.name: Net gain/loss on fair value changes
products.note: Any difference between the fair value and the carrying amount of the asset and are recognised in the Statement of profit and loss when the asset is derecognised.

products.name: Income from assignment transactions
products.note: The transfer of financial assets qualifies for derecognition in its entirety, the whole of the interest spread at its present value (discounted over the behavioural tenure of the asset) is recognized on the date of derecognition.

products.name: Other operational revenue
products.note: Other operational revenue represents income earned from the activities incidental to the business and is recognized when the right to receive the income is established as per the terms of the contract.

outlook.statement: As we enter FY2027, we do so with confidence and clarity of purpose. Backed by a diversified business model and a strong balance sheet, we are well positioned to capture emerging opportunities and create enduring value.

Unity Bank will continue to strengthen its deposit base through targeted cross-selling initiatives and strategic aggregator partnerships, and focus on scaling new growth drivers such as personal loans, commercial banking, credit cards and gold loans, alongside diversification into secured segments such as affordable housing.

The Group will continue to focus on disciplined growth, deepening client relationships, leveraging technology and driving cross-business synergies to build a sustainable and agile financial services platform.

Unity Bank is evaluating new initiatives such as Credit Line on UPI as well as secured credit cards. The recently received AD-I license will support additional fee income streams through forex and cross-border services.
Investment Banking business is well positioned for sustained growth with a healthy pipeline of transactions across IPOs, QIPs and capital market transactions.
Modulus Alternatives is well positioned for its next phase of growth with the launch of Fund III (ICOF III, target Rs 2,000+ Cr).
Roarbank achievement reinforces customer confidence and sets the stage for faster, bigger growth in the months ahead
Detailed business review & outlook appended in Management Discussion and Analysis section

India's wealth management opportunity remains large, structurally durable and in early stages of evolution; long-term tailwinds include rising affluence, increasing financialisation of savings, maturing regulatory framework and accelerating generational transfer of wealth
B30 and Tier-II markets expected to generate AUM growth opportunity of approximately ₹1.6 trillion by FY2029

FY26 begins with Indian equities entering relatively balanced phase; first half expected to remain volatile amid global uncertainties, second half expected to see stronger earnings momentum and more stable growth-oriented market environment
India's alternative investments industry AUM projected to reach USD 247 billion by 2029
Modulus enters FY27 with strong institutional platform; immediate priority is successful fundraising and deployment of India Credit Opportunities Fund III (ICOF III)

Unity Small Finance Bank remains focused on executing long-term growth agenda; committed to serving 10 million underserved customers by 2029; will continue investing in technology and scaling business through agentic AI-based solutions
